admission_rules_intro: Before submitting your application, you must read and accept the village coexistence rules ({{count}} rules).
admission_rules_accept: I have read and accept the Village Law: duties, prohibitions, offenses and admission process. I understand that non-compliance may lead to sanctions or expulsion.
gov_no_rules_desc: Governance rules will be published when the assembly approves them.
gov_default_subtitle: Coexistence rules approved by the General Assembly. These norms govern community life: government structure, duties, permissions, prohibitions, offenses and admission and exit processes.
gov_rules_count: {{count}} rules in effect - Any modification requires General Assembly approval
gov_three_levels_desc: The system has three levels. Each is internally independent but subject to the higher level. The rules below are for Level 2 (Village). Level 1 (Federation) and Level 3 (Organizations) are managed separately.
gov_level1_desc: Decisions affecting all nodes worldwide. By vote of all nodes. E.g.: TQ basic basket, node expulsion, communication protocol.
gov_level2_desc: Decisions affecting the entire local community. By node assembly. E.g.: wages, schedules, catalog, admission, fees, coexistence rules.
gov_level3_desc: Decisions affecting only within each organization. By internal assembly. E.g.: internal rules, departments, roles. Subject to village rules.
gov_fed_levels_desc: Each node in the federation goes through three trust levels. The level determines the credit limit, voting rights and the ability to sponsor new nodes.
gov_fed_l1_items: Limit of 1,000 TQ|No voting rights in the federation|Cannot sponsor (be godfather of) new nodes|Access to the multilateral global pool|Minimum 90-day period before being eligible for promotion
gov_fed_l2_items: Limit of 5,000 TQ|Voting rights in federation decisions|Can sponsor (be godfather of) new nodes|Full access to the multilateral global pool|Achieved after a federation-wide vote (minimum 90 days at level 1)
gov_fed_l3_items: Limit of 20,000 TQ|Voting rights and sponsorship capacity|Full access to the multilateral global pool|Automatic promotion upon meeting reciprocity and required average limit
gov_fed_promotion: Promotion to Level 2: Requires a federation-wide vote after a minimum of 90 days as a New Node. Promotion to Level 3 is automatic when the node meets the reciprocity requirements and the federation's average limit.
gov_sponsor_desc: Nodes at level 2 or higher can sponsor new nodes joining the federation, assuming solidarity responsibility for their debt in case of default.
gov_sponsor_how_items: Only Level 2 (Accepted) or Level 3 (Full) nodes can be godfathers|When sponsoring a new node, the godfather's limit is reduced by the sponsored node's limit amount (1,000 TQ)|The sponsored node enters as Level 1 (New Node) with its 1,000 TQ limit|If the sponsored node defaults, the debt transfers to the godfather|When the sponsored node reaches Level 2, the godfather's retained limit is automatically released
gov_sponsor_resp_items: The godfather is jointly liable for the sponsored node's debt|The godfather's effective limit = nominal limit - sum of sponsored nodes' limits|A node can sponsor multiple new nodes, as long as it has available limit|Sponsorship fosters trust: the godfather only sponsors nodes it knows and trusts|Releasing the limit when the godchild reaches Level 2 incentivizes the godfather to support the new node's growth
gov_pool_title: Multilateral Global Pool vs. Bilateral Pools
gov_pool_desc: The federation manages two types of balance pools: a shared global pool and bilateral pools between pairs of nodes.
gov_pool_global_desc: A pool shared by all federated nodes. The balance you earn in node B is spendable in node C. That is, if a user from node A buys products from a producer in node B, the positive balance generated by node B's producer can be used to buy products from node C. This enables real multilateral barter between all federated communities, not just peer-to-peer.
gov_pool_bilateral_desc: Each pair of nodes also maintains an independent bilateral balance. This balance reflects direct exchange between two specific nodes. Bilateral pools are separate from the global pool: the bilateral balance with node B does not mix with the bilateral balance with node C. Previously, the system only checked bilateral limits; now a real global pool exists that enables full multilateralism.
gov_verify_desc: For greater security, POS terminal pairing and new node incorporation into the federation use a 4-option verification system.
gov_verify_steps: The device or node requesting pairing generates a 6-digit code|The confirmer (receiving node administrator) sees 4 code options on screen|Only one of the 4 options is the correct code shown by the requesting device|The confirmer must select the correct code from the 4 options|If they select the wrong code, the pairing is automatically rejected
gov_verify_note: This system prevents man-in-the-middle attacks: even if an attacker intercepts communication, they cannot force approval without visually knowing which of the 4 options is correct.
gov_integrity_desc: Transactions between federated nodes are protected by a double-signature and chained hash system that guarantees their integrity.
gov_integrity_double_desc: Each transaction between federated nodes requires the cryptographic signature of both nodes (sender and receiver). This means no node can forge a transaction on behalf of the other. Both parties must cryptographically confirm the transaction for it to be valid.
gov_integrity_hash_desc: Transactions between nodes are chained through hashes: each transaction includes the hash of the previous transaction. This creates an immutable chain where any modification of a past transaction invalidates all subsequent ones. It allows verifying the complete integrity of the exchange history between two nodes.
gov_footer: These rules are binding for all village members. To request modifications, contact the Board of Directors or submit a proposal at the next General Assembly.
gov_modal_approved_notice: This rule was approved by the General Assembly. It cannot be edited directly. Your proposal will be sent as a governance modification proposal for the assembly to debate and vote on.
gov_modal_placeholder: E.g.: Modify the initial credit limit from 500 TQ to 800 TQ because the cost of living has increased...
gov_modal_error_empty: Error: describe the change you propose
gov_modal_success: Proposal sent to the Assembly. It will be debated at the next session.
gov_modal_error_send: Error: could not send the proposal
fed_hero_badge: Free Platform for Ecovillages and Communities
fed_hero_subtitle: A free and configurable system that allows each ecovillage to manage its economy, governance and exchanges, and federate with other communities in a network of fair trade, without inflation and without intermediaries.
fed_what_desc1: Imagine what Visa and Mastercard do for merchants in different countries: grouping them into a network that allows borderless exchange. Now imagine that, but for ecovillages, self-managed communities and barter networks. Each community maintains its autonomy, its rules and its governance, but can trade with other federated communities fairly.
fed_what_desc2: The Federated Exchange Network platform allows each ecovillage to have:
fed_what_features: Configurable governance|Each community defines its own rules, assemblies, quorum, member levels and admission processes.|Own economy|Community currency (TQ) based on energy (kWh/Joule), not on bank money. No inflation, no interest.|Federation between nodes|Trade with other federated ecovillages. Each node respects the internal rules of others.|Self-managed community|Organizations, departments, assemblies, voting, member admission and account recovery.|Public website|Each node has its own configurable website to showcase products, philosophy and contact info.|Free and open|The platform is free. Consulting included. Open to contributions and improvements from real experience.
fed_benefits_items: More merchants available|The more ecovillages federate, the more versatile and independent the network. Each ecovillage has its own trade system, but can exchange with all the others.|No inflation|The TQ community currency is based on real energy consumption (kWh/Joule), not on arbitrary issuance. There is no inflation because there is no money creation without backing.|Total autonomy|Each community maintains its rules, its governance and its autonomy. The federation does not interfere in each node's internal decisions.|Fair trade|Exchange without intermediaries. Prices are calculated based on energy, not speculation. Each product has an objective value.|Federated identity|Each member identifies with their documents (ID card, passport, etc.). When federating two nodes, duplicates are detected and both assemblies decides how to resolve.|Free with consulting|The platform is free. Includes consulting to implement the system in your ecovillage. No hidden costs.
fed_unified_title: Why work on a unified codebase
fed_unified_desc: We have never advanced by working in isolation. Each person creating their own system may perhaps unify small groups within their country, but if we want worldwide unification, there must be things that are common.
fed_unified_card1_desc: All software is 100% open source. Anyone can audit, modify and adapt it to their reality. But the core —communication between nodes and the barter currency— must be the same for everyone. Improvements implemented in the central code are available to all. If Uruguay adds a feature, Venezuela can use it. If Venezuela improves something, Uruguay benefits.
fed_unified_card2_title: Your card works at any node
fed_unified_card2_desc: Like Visa or Mastercard: no matter what country or node you're in, your NFC card should be accepted immediately, applying the unified protocol limits instantly. If each country invents its own protocol, cards from one country won't work in another, destroying the federation.
fed_unified_card3_desc: 1 TQ = 1 kWh of real physical energy. Energy has no nationality. If each country invents its own metric, we fall into the traditional currency market with exchange speculation. The metric must be universal and collectively audited by the software so that inter-node trade is fair.
fed_unified_card4_desc: Those who know how to program write code. Those who don't, audit it, understand it, and accept or reject changes in human language. New implementations are explained so everyone understands them. This way we support each other: what one invents, is made available to all.
fed_unified_amber_title: It can be developed in another language, but...
fed_unified_amber_p1: It's not that separate software can't be used. Anyone can develop the same functionality in whatever language they want. But they must guarantee that their code can correctly communicate with all implementations of the base code. It must be 100% compatible. The idea is that we all work on a base code that we all know exists, audit it, and then each person can change the skin, colors, the language it was written in —but the internal engine and communication are exactly the same.
fed_unified_amber_p2:
What can be modified locally without approval: product catalog, internal governance rules, website colors, local reference currency, installed services, cultural adaptations, trading hours.

What requires approval from all nodes: inter-node communication protocol, barter currency value metric, NFC card cryptographic protocol, ledger structure, node expulsion rules.
fed_gov_desc: The system has three levels of governance, each internally independent but subject to the higher level. The broadest rules encompass the most common things among everyone. Each organization's rules only affect within its own scope. Universal rules affect the entire world.
fed_gov_l1_desc: Decisions that affect ALL nodes in the world. Decided by equal voting of all federated nodes.
fed_gov_l1_items: TQ basic basket (same everywhere)|Global credit limit|Node expulsion|Communication protocol|Barter currency metric|NFC cryptographic protocol
fed_gov_l1_note:
Why the basket is federated: The barter currency has no inflation, so the basket must be exactly the same everywhere. If one country has a higher basket and another lower, wealth is created on one side and poverty on the other.

This has nothing to do with foreign trade: Each node does its foreign trade directly in its local currency (UYU, VES, ARS). The Conversion Factor calculates the TQ equivalent, but that's internal to each node.
fed_gov_l2_desc: Decisions that affect the entire local community. Decided by the node's assembly. Each node is sovereign.
fed_gov_l2_items: Work hours and wages|Local product catalog|Internal governance rules|Member admission|Foreign trade (local currency)|Hours, rates, commissions|Public website|Cultural adaptations
fed_gov_l2_note: What the village decides cannot affect the federated basic basket. Work hours, wages and foreign trade are internal to the node.
fed_gov_l3_desc: Decisions that affect only within the organization. Decided by the organization's assembly. A node can have multiple organizations.
fed_gov_l3_items: Internal organization rules|Internal departments|Organization assemblies|Internal roles and permissions
fed_gov_l3_note: Each organization is independent within its own scope, but is subject to the general rules of the village.
fed_gov_consensus_desc: One node proposes a change. All federated nodes review it and approve or reject it. By default, 100% is needed (everyone). When consensus is reached, the change is applied automatically everywhere. If not reached, the current value continues to be used. The threshold can be changed, but changing it requires approval under the current threshold. This way no one imposes rules unilaterally.
fed_pool_desc: The federation has two ways of managing balance between nodes. This is something new that didn't exist before: previously there were only bilateral limits between two nodes. Now there is a real global pool shared by all.
fed_pool_global_desc: A shared balance among all federated nodes. If you trade with node B and earn a balance, you can spend it at node C. It's not tied to a single node. The limit depends on the node's level (see below).
fed_pool_global_example: Example: You buy seeds from node B (negative global balance). Then you sell fruits to node C (positive global balance). The balance is automatically compensated in the shared pool.
fed_pool_bilateral_desc: Specific agreements between two nodes. The bilateral balance only applies between those two nodes. Does not affect the global pool. Useful when two nodes want a higher limit than normal for their trade.
fed_pool_bilateral_example: Example: Node A and node B agree on a bilateral limit of 10000 TQ. Their transactions go to the bilateral pool, not the global one.
fed_pool_which_title: How it's decided which pool to use
fed_pool_which_desc: If there's an active bilateral agreement between the two nodes, the transaction goes to the bilateral pool. If there's no bilateral agreement, it goes to the global pool. Bilateral transactions never affect the global pool and vice versa.
fed_node_levels_desc: Federation nodes have levels that determine their permissions, limits and rights. This is different from member levels within a node: these levels apply to the nodes themselves within the world federation.
fed_nl1_desc: Newly joined node to the federation. Has a voice (can opine) but has no vote on federated proposals and cannot sponsor new nodes. Must remain at least 90 days before requesting a level upgrade.
fed_nl1_items: Can trade with the global pool|Has a voice in the federation|Cannot vote on federated proposals|Cannot sponsor new nodes
fed_nl2_desc: Node approved by federated assembly. With voting rights on federated proposals and can sponsor new nodes (act as godparent). Must remain at least 180 days before being able to rise to level 3.
fed_nl2_items: Can vote on federated proposals|Can sponsor new nodes|Higher limit in the global pool|Participates in federated decisions
fed_nl3_desc: Fully trusted node. Automatic upgrade from level 2 if it meets: minimum 180 days at level 2, reciprocity (both contributes and receives), and average limit higher than half the current limit. An inactive node does not qualify.
fed_nl3_items: Highest global pool limit|Automatic upgrade with reciprocity|Can sponsor and vote|Requires real reciprocal activity
fed_nl_promotion_desc:
Level 1 to level 2: Requires federated voting (all nodes with voting rights decides). Cannot be proposed before the minimum configured days have passed. Upon rising to level 2, the godparent's retained limit is released.

Level 2 to level 3: Automatic if it meets reciprocity + average limit. Does not require voting. A node that only sends or only receives does not qualify: it must demonstrate real reciprocal activity.
fed_sponsor_desc: When a new node wants to join the federation, it doesn't join alone. It needs a godparent: a level 2+ node that backs it and is responsible for it.
fed_sponsor_how_items: 1. A level 2+ node agrees to be the godparent of the new node|2. The new node enters at level 1 with its limit (e.g.: 1000 TQ)|3. The godparent's limit is reduced by the same amount|4. The godparent is responsible for the new node|5. If the new node defaults, the debt passes to the godparent|6. When the node rises to level 2, the godparent's limit is released
fed_sponsor_example_desc: Node A (level 2, limit 5000 TQ) sponsors node B (new, 1000 TQ).
fed_sponsor_example_items: A's normal limit: 5000 TQ|B's sponsorship: -1000 TQ|A's effective limit: 4000 TQ|A can sponsor up to 4 nodes (5000 / 1000 = 4)|If B rises to level 2, A recovers its 1000 TQ|If B defaults, A assumes B's debt
fed_sponsor_why_desc: Prevents any node from entering the federation without responsibility. The godparent risks their own limit and is responsible for the new node. This prevents uncontrolled admission of nodes that might not fulfill their commitments.
fed_verify_desc: To join the federation or pair a POS terminal, we use a verification system that forces out-of-band communication (by phone, message, in person).
fed_verify_s1_title: The new node generates a code
fed_verify_s1_desc: The new node initiates the request and obtains a 6-digit code.
fed_verify_s2_desc: 4 codes appear on the godparent's screen. Only one is correct.
fed_verify_s3_desc: The new node tells the correct code to the godparent by phone, message or in person.
fed_verify_s4_title: The godparent picks the correct one
fed_verify_s4_desc: If they pick correctly, the node joins the federation. If wrong, it's rejected. The code expires in 60 seconds.
fed_verify_why_title: Why 4 options and not just show the code
fed_verify_why_desc: If both sides see the same code on screen, a man-in-the-middle attacker could intercept the connection and show the same fake code to both. With 4 options, the attacker doesn't know which is correct: they have to guess (25% probability). Forcing the code to be communicated through another channel (phone) means the attacker can't fool either side.
fed_integrity_desc: Each node has its own database and can function without internet. How do we guarantee that inter-node transactions are valid and nobody cheats? With dual signing and chained hashes.
fed_integrity_dual_desc: Each inter-node transaction must be signed by BOTH nodes with their cryptographic keys. Node A creates and signs the transaction. Node B verifies A's signature, also signs, and returns the dual-signed transaction. A transaction without both signatures is not valid. No node can create a unilateral obligation.
fed_integrity_hash_desc: Each transaction includes the hash of the previous transaction (like a simplified blockchain). If someone tries to insert, modify or delete a transaction, the chain breaks and is immediately detected. When reconnecting two nodes, they compare their hashes and synchronize any divergence.
fed_integrity_recon_desc: When a node that was offline reconnects, it compares the hashes of its chain with the other node's. If they match, they're synchronized. If not, they exchange divergent transactions, verify signatures and hashes, and incorporate valid ones. Invalid ones are audited. This guarantees both nodes have the same view of transactions, without needing a central database.
fed_features_title: What does the system currently include?
fed_features_list: Member management and levels|Admission requests with documents|Assemblies and voting|Organizations and departments|Exchanges and mutual credit (TQ)|Product catalog with energy prices|Android POS app (QR + NFC payment)|Web POS for iPhone/computers|ESP32 terminals (keypad, touch, communal)|Bluetooth NFC reader (POS accessory)|Short code pairing|Notifications (WebPush, XMPP, SMS, Telegram)|Accounting and auditing|Account recovery (multisig)|Inter-node federation|Global multilateral pool (shared balance)|Bilateral pools (agreements between two nodes)|Federated node levels (New, Accepted, Full)|Godparent system (responsible sponsor)|4-option verification (anti-MITM)|Dual signing + chained hash (integrity)|Automatic reconciliation on reconnect|Configurable public website|Configurable governance per node|Federated governance between nodes|Foreign trade with 20 local currencies|Energy-based price calculator|Federated basic basket (same value everywhere)|Encrypted parallel internet (WireGuard)|Off-grid local intranet (OpenWrt)|One-click federated services (Matrix, Nextcloud, VoIP, +20)|Automatic installer with wizard|Demo node that restarts every 24h
fed_propose_desc: The system is under continuous development. If you have an ecovillage or community, tell us what you need. If you see something missing, propose it. If you have experience, share it. The most voted proposals will be prioritized.
fed_propose_form_desc_ph: Describe your proposal in detail. What problem does it solve? How would you imagine it working?
fed_propose_success: Proposal submitted. Thank you for contributing!
fed_share_desc: If you know someone who wants to create an ecovillage or already has one, share this message on social media.
fed_share_message:
The biggest challenge of creating an ecovillage? It's not buying the land... it's reaching agreement. 🏡🤝

Many eco-friendly and intentional projects fail because they lack solid governance and economic foundations. That's why I've developed a universal, modular and decentralized digital system specifically designed to solve this and bring real order to any ecovillage in the world.

What is the project about?

🌐 Autonomy + Federation: Each ecovillage functions as an independent node with its own laws, culture and assemblies. But by federating with other nodes, they can trade with each other fairly and safely using technologies like QR codes and NFC cards.

🗳️ Governance and Digital Assembly: Forget about community paralysis or informal agreements that break down. The platform features a Digital Assembly and transparent Voting system to debate, propose changes and record decisions immutably.

🔋 TQ Barter (Inflation-Immune Currency): We use a mutual credit accounting system where the unit of measure is not tied to the dollar or gold, but to the laws of physics: 1 TQ = 1 kWh of work, harvest or inputs.

🚜 Real Wealth Accumulation vs. Fake Numbers: Unlike capitalism that tricks you into accumulating virtual numbers on a screen that the bank can freeze or inflation can devalue, our system motivates you to accumulate real and tangible wealth (your bioclimatic home, gardens, tools, seeds or a tractor).

📈 Dynamic Limits: Credit limits are not fixed or restrictive; they are steps of trust. A new member starts with a protective limit equivalent to their basic family basket and this rises in assembly as they integrate and contribute to the community.

Do you have an ecovillage, land, or want to found one? My platform is under active development and I want it to be a tool that perfectly adapts to each community's needs. I'm very interested in talking with people who have experiences (both positive and negative) to learn, improve the software and show you a demonstration of how it works.

📩 Message me privately to show you the system, learn about your experience and see how we can join this Federated Ecovillage Network. Let's make sustainable communities an organized reality! 🌾✨
fed_demo_title: Want to see the system from the inside?
fed_demo_desc: We have a demo node that's complete and functional: a system with sample data (users, organizations, products, transactions) so you can explore everything freely. It doesn't affect the real node. It restarts every 24 hours.
fed_demo_preset_desc: Choose the data the demo will start with. Each profile loads different users, organizations and rules.
fed_demo_start_msg_timeout: Timeout: demo didn't respond in 4 minutes
fed_demo_start_msg_connect: Could not connect to node to verify status
fed_demo_status_running: The demo node is active. Enter and explore freely.
fed_demo_status_stopped: The demo node is not running to save resources. Press the button to start it. It takes a few seconds to boot.
fed_demo_restart_note: It stops automatically every 24 hours. Each time it restarts, it starts from scratch with fresh data.
fed_demo_features_title: The demo node has its own complete system:
fed_models_desc: The idea is to be 100% transparent. Share, not hoard advantages. If someone invents something that works, they make it available to others. That's why we use a federated network of villages: we share experiences, governance that has given us success, and the code.
fed_models_card1_desc: Someone new comes, analyzes existing villages: what their internal governance is, how it works, and can copy the model to implement in their own village without starting from scratch and making mistakes.
fed_models_card2_desc: Each node can add new implementations and modules. Other nodes can view them, download them and use them too. What you invent, others can copy to their own node.
fed_models_card3_desc: Code is created completely clean so anyone can adapt it to their reality. All code should have in settings the option to change the default node, so people from any node can use it.
fed_faq_title: Frequently Asked Questions about the Federation
fed_faq_desc: We answer the most common questions about how the federated community network works, barter, and how to join.
fed_faq_q_1: What's the point of federating? Isn't it better for each community to function alone?
fed_faq_a_1: Each community is autonomous and makes its own internal decisions. But federating has advantages: you can trade with members of other communities, the spectrum of what you can contribute and receive expands, and communities support each other. A lone community is fragile; a network of communities is robust. If one community has problems, others can help.
fed_faq_q_2: Do I have to contribute something to join a federated community?
fed_faq_a_2: Yes. This is the most important rule: to join you must have something to contribute. It can be products, work, talents, services, or knowledge. If you only want to receive but have nothing to contribute, barter won't work for you. Many community currencies fail because too many people join who only want to receive and few who contribute. So before joining, ask yourself: What do I have that the community might need? What does the community have that I might need? If both answers are positive, it's worth joining.
fed_faq_q_3: Why is the perfect balance zero?
fed_faq_a_3: The goal of every member is for their balance to be zero. If your balance is at zero, it means you've contributed to the community exactly the same as you've received from it. That's equilibrium. If your balance is very negative, you're receiving a lot but contributing little: you need to contribute more. If it's very positive, you're contributing a lot but not taking advantage of what the community offers. Zero balance is everyone's goal.
fed_faq_q_4: What if I only want to receive from the community but have nothing to contribute?
fed_faq_a_4: Barter doesn't work that way. Barter requires both sides to gain: you contribute something and receive something in return. If you join with nothing to contribute, you'd only be receiving from others without giving back. That unbalances the system and isn't fair. If you want to consume market products without being a member, you can come as a visitor and buy in local currency. To be a barter member, you need to contribute.
fed_faq_q_5: Can I use my TQ balance in another community in the federation?
fed_faq_a_5: Yes. That's one of the advantages of federation. If you go to another federated community, you can use your NFC card or your account to trade. But remember: the balance remains the same. If you spend in another community, your balance goes down. The federation doesn't create new money, it only expands the spectrum of what you can receive.
fed_faq_q_6: Does my community have to use the same software as the others?
fed_faq_a_6: Yes, all federated communities use the same base software because it's the only way to guarantee that exchanges work correctly between communities. But each community can customize the colors, texts, language, and internal rules of their platform. The technical base is shared, but each community's identity is their own. The software is open source, so anyone can audit and adapt it.
fed_faq_q_7: What happens while there are few federated communities?
fed_faq_a_7: At first, with few communities, the spectrum of what you can contribute and receive is more limited. That's why it's crucial that each community that federates ensures its members have something real to contribute. As more communities federate, the spectrum expands: more products, more services, more places to contribute work, more things to receive. The federation becomes stronger the more communities participate.
fed_faq_a_8: The federation is governed by voting of all federated nodes. Each community (node) has one vote. Decisions that affect the entire federation (such as the TQ basic basket, global credit limit, or expulsion of a problematic node) are made collectively. No community can impose rules on the others.
fed_faq_q_9: Does the TQ currency have inflation?
fed_faq_a_9: No. The TQ currency has no inflation because it's not tied to any country's money or gold. It's tied to energy: 1 TQ = 1 kWh. Energy doesn't devalue. An hour of work today is worth the same as an hour of work 10 years from now. This means what you save in TQ maintains its real value over time, unlike money in the bank that loses value every month due to inflation.
fed_faq_q_10: Can I accumulate TQ to get rich?
fed_faq_a_10: The system isn't designed for anyone to get rich accumulating numbers. The goal is equilibrium: contributing and receiving in similar proportion. Accumulating a lot of TQ means you're contributing a lot but not taking advantage of what the community offers. Instead of accumulating TQ, we invite you to accumulate real and tangible wealth: your home, your garden, your tools, your seeds, your community relationships. That is real wealth.
fed_faq_q_11: Are public sales mixed with barter?
fed_faq_a_11: No! General public sales are external and paid in the country's local currency (pesos, bolivars, etc.). TQ barter is only among registered members. External buyers don't have TQ accounts or participate in barter. This is very important: we can't mix public sales with barter, because they're different things with different rules.
fed_faq_q_12: How do I know if it's worth joining a federated community?
fed_faq_a_12: Ask yourself these three questions: 1) Do I have something to contribute that the community might need? (products, work, talents, services). 2) Does the community have something I need or am interested in? (food, work, services, connection with people). 3) Am I willing to participate actively, not just receive? If all three answers are yes, it's worth joining. If you only want to receive but have nothing to contribute, barter won't work for you.
fed_faq_q_13: What can I contribute besides products?
fed_faq_a_13: You can contribute products (fruits, vegetables, eggs, breads, crafts, preserves, natural medicine), services (repairs, transport, classes, childcare, hairdressing), work (helping in gardens, construction, cleaning, event organization), or knowledge (workshops, consulting, mentoring). Everything the community values can be a contribution. It doesn't have to be just material things: time and talent also count.
fed_faq_q_14: Do I need to have land or a garden to join?
fed_faq_a_14: Not necessarily. There are members who are producers with land, but there are also artisans, bakers, herbalists, people who offer services, and people who contribute their labor in others' gardens. What matters is not what you have, but what you can contribute with what you have.
fed_faq_q_15: What happens if my balance goes very negative?
fed_faq_a_15: If your balance drops too low, the system notifies you. You need to contribute more (sell products, offer labor, give workshops) to raise your balance. If you can't raise it, the assembly can review your case. The idea isn't to punish, but to help you find balance. But if a person only receives and never contributes, the assembly can decides they can no longer stay in the system.
fed_faq_q_16: Can I leave the community whenever I want?
fed_faq_a_16: Yes. Ideally, before leaving, your balance should be at or near zero. If your balance is very negative (you received more than you contributed), the assembly may ask you to contribute something before leaving to balance your account. If your balance is positive, you simply lose that balance upon leaving, since TQ has no value outside the community.
fed_faq_q_17: Does the federation work without internet?
fed_faq_a_17: The federation can work in two ways: via public Internet (when communities are far apart) or via community intranet using WireGuard tunnels (when they're nearby and don't depend on public Internet). This means even communities without Internet access can federate if they install OpenWrt and configure the tunnels.
fed_faq_q_18: Does my community have to pay to use the software?
fed_faq_a_18: No. The software is 100% free and open source. Any community can install, use, and adapt it without paying licenses. All you need is a server (can be a modest computer) and someone with basic IT knowledge for installation. The developer community helps with initial setup.
